Please solve this issue: You are working on Campfire, a chat application written in Rust (a port of the Rails app, compatible with its database). Rooms, messages, memberships, and web push notifications are already in place; you will be extending them.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Some bots misbehave: they flood rooms, or their webhooks keep failing.

> As an administrator, I want misbehaving bots to be stopped automatically,
> and I want to decide when they come back.

Flooding:

- A bot may post at most 10 messages in any 10 seconds. Messages posted through the API and webhook replies both count.
- The message that goes over the limit is rejected and starts a 30-second cooldown. During the cooldown, the posting endpoint responds with `429 Too Many Requests` and a `Retry-After` header (seconds left), and webhook replies are not posted.
- Five more attempts to post during the same cooldown suspend the bot.

Failing webhooks:

- A failed delivery is any response other than `2xx`, a timeout, or a connection error.
- Ten failed deliveries in a row suspend the bot. A successful delivery resets the count.

A suspended bot:

- gets `403 Forbidden` from the posting endpoint;
- receives no webhooks;
- keeps its rooms and messages, and still counts towards its owner's bot limit;
- stays listed on the bots page and shows as "Suspended", with the reason.

Only administrators can reactivate a suspended bot, from the bots page: a "Reactivate" button that asks for confirmation. The limits above are fixed in code; they have no settings.

## Data

- A bot is a `users` row with `role = 2` (`Role::Bot`), so it joins rooms, has memberships and
  authors messages like a person. Unlike a person's, `User::create` doesn't grant it the open
  rooms: see "Rooms" below.
- Its `bots` row (`campfire_db::Bot`, created by `schema::ADDITIONS`) holds `user_id` (unique),
  `creator_id` and `token`. It's a separate table rather than columns on `users`:
  `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is idempotent on every boot, `users` keeps the Rails columns that
  `columns_test` checks, and the Rails image ignores it.
- The bot code is `"<user id>-<token>"` (Rails Campfire's `bot_key` format). The token has 24
  alphanumeric characters. `Bot::authenticate` looks the bot up by id and compares tokens with
  `rails_compat::secure_compare`.
- `password_digest` is `NOT NULL`, so a bot gets the bcrypt digest of a random password. It has no
  email address, so it can't sign in, and session transfers refuse bots.
- Deleting a bot deletes its `bots` row (and its webhook) and deactivates its user, so its messages
  keep their author. Resetting a code (`PATCH /bots/:bot_id/key`) replaces the token.
- A bot's optional webhook is a `bot_webhooks` row (`campfire_db::Webhook`: `bot_id` unique, `url`),
  another `schema::ADDITIONS` table: a column added to `bots` wouldn't reach databases that already
  have the table. `Webhook::assign` strips the URL, deletes the row for a blank one, and otherwise
  validates an absolute `http(s)://` URL with a host (error on `webhook_url`) and upserts.

## Rooms

- A bot is in the rooms people add it to (closed rooms' member pickers, direct rooms), and in
  every open room when the form's "Add to all open rooms" switch (`bot[all_open_rooms]`, a
  `check_box` with its hidden `"0"`, off by default) is on. A missing or blank key leaves the
  setting as it is.
- The switch is a `bots_in_all_open_rooms` row (`bot_id` unique), another `schema::ADDITIONS`
  table. `Bot::update_all_open_rooms(true)` upserts it and, after commit, grants the bot every
  open room (`room::grant_open_rooms_to`); `false` deletes it and leaves the memberships alone.
  Deleting a bot deletes the row.
- `Rooms::Open`'s grant to everyone (`room::grant_to_active_users`, on create and on becoming
  open) takes the active people and only the bots with that row.
- Every membership insert goes through `room::insert_memberships`, which `RETURNING "user_id"`s
  the rows it actually created (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` skips existing members) and emits
  `Event::BotJoined { room_id, user_id }` for the bots among them, unless the room is direct. So
  `joined` fires exactly once per membership: re-saving a room or switching the setting on again
  sends nothing, and a bot removed and added back joins again.

## Routes

`controllers::app_routes` holds routes Rails doesn't have. They're matched after the whole Rails
table, which stays identical to `vectors/campfire_routes.json`. The route tests seed their corpus
from both tables.

| Route | Action |
|---|---|
| `GET /bots`, `GET /bots/new`, `POST /bots` | list (no pagination, `Cache-Control: no-store`), form, create |
| `GET /bots/:id/edit`, `PATCH/PUT /bots/:id`, `DELETE /bots/:id` | edit, rename/webhook/avatar, delete |
| `PATCH/PUT /bots/:bot_id/key` | new code |
| `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages` | the bot API (`messages::by_bots`) |

Bots someone can't manage answer 404 (`Bot::find_manageable_by`).

## The bot API

- The chain skips session authentication and forgery protection. `concerns::authenticate_bot`
  returns 401, then `set_room` returns 404 (an unknown room, or one the bot isn't in). A blank body
  without a multipart `attachment` gets 422. Success is `201` with `Location: /messages/:id`, a path.
- The raw body is the rich-text body, as Rails Campfire's `request.body.read` is. HTML is sanitized
  on render. Creating, broadcasting and push use the composer's `create_message` and
  `broadcast_create`.
- `curl -d` sends `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. kit would reject bodies like `100% done` as
  malformed params before routing. `by_bots::read_raw_body`, a middleware in `app::router`, parses
  the body for this path and drops param errors.
- `by_bots::filter_key` is the `PathFilter` that `KitConfig::filter_logged_path` and
  `FrontConfig::filter_logged_path` use, so request logs show the code as `[FILTERED]`.

  keeps the name the item's only text, so `getByText(name)` stays unambiguous. No other control's
  accessible name contains "bot code".

**Flooding**
- A bot may post 10 messages in any 10 seconds. The limit counts the bot's own messages, so posts through the API and webhook replies both count.
- The check runs in the same database transaction that creates the message. Several posts arriving at once can't all slip under the limit.
- The 11th post gets `429` with `Retry-After: 30` and starts a 30-second cooldown. Each post during the cooldown gets `429` with the seconds left, rounded up.
- The fifth attempt during a cooldown suspends the bot. A new cooldown starts the count again.
- During a cooldown the bot still receives webhooks, but its replies aren't posted.

**Failing webhooks**
- A non-2xx response, a timeout or a connection error counts as a failure. Ten in a row suspend the bot, and a successful delivery resets the count.
- A 2xx reply that is too large to post counts as a success, because the delivery itself worked.

**Suspended bots**
- The posting endpoint returns `403` straight after the bot code is checked, before the room is looked up.
- A suspended bot gets no webhooks: neither mention nor joined.
- It keeps its rooms and messages, still counts towards its owner's bot limit, and stays listed on the bots page.
- The bots page shows "Suspended" with the reason. Administrators see a "Reactivate" button, which asks for confirmation through the browser's native `confirm()`. It sends `DELETE /bots/:bot_id/suspension`; anyone else who tries that gets `403`. Reactivating also clears the cooldown and failure count, so the bot starts afresh.

**Decisions you may want to revisit**
- The fifth attempt that suspends a bot still answers `429`, since it happens during the cooldown. The next post gets `403`.
- A webhook reply during a cooldown counts as one of the five attempts, the same as an API post.

**Storage**
- I added two new tables, `bot_throttles` and `bot_suspensions`, so cooldowns and suspensions survive a restart.
- I added an index on `messages` (`creator_id`, `created_at`) so counting a bot's recent messages stays cheap.
- All three are additions that the Rails app ignores. The limits are constants in `crates/db/src/models/throttle.rs`, with no settings.
